rows.verified: HSE electrical guidance addresses planning, management and control of electrical systems and equipment on construction sites.
The guidance explains measures intended to reduce accidents involving electricity.
Safe-working advice applies across design, specification, selection, installation, commissioning, maintenance and operation.
HSE links construction electrical controls to CDM 2015, the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 and PUWER 1998.
Specific HSE guidance is provided for avoiding danger from overhead power lines.
Specific HSE guidance is provided for avoiding danger from underground services.
Safe isolation procedures are a key part of managing low-voltage electrical work.
HSE's simple precautions and frequently asked questions help dutyholders select appropriate electrical guidance.
Electrical risk depends on voltage, system condition, isolation, earthing, environment, buried or overhead services, task, competence and supervision.
HSE electrical evidence is installation-, task-, equipment-, environment-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level electrocution probability.
HSE states that construction dust is a real lung risk rather than only a nuisance.
COSHH requires hazardous construction dust risks to be assessed, controlled and reviewed.
Regular exposure can contribute to lung cancer, asthma, COPD and silicosis.
Silica occurs in rocks, sand and clay and in construction materials including bricks and concrete.
Respirable crystalline silica is fine enough to penetrate deeply into the lungs and may be invisible in normal lighting.
Dry sweeping concrete dust can create high airborne dust levels and should be avoided where possible.
Task controls include water suppression, on-tool extraction and suitable respiratory protective equipment.
Health surveillance must be provided where workers are regularly exposed and there is a reasonable likelihood of silicosis.
Construction-dust risk depends on material, task, tool energy, duration, enclosure, ventilation, extraction, water suppression, RPE fit and maintenance.
HSE construction-dust evidence is material-, task-, worker-, exposure-, control-, environment- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
